about: The stock sites the Modwerk base owns and turns into events, and the tables modules contribute to (EVENTS.md). Modules subscribe or contribute; none patches these sites. events.py generates the base's dispatch, the loader's table header, the SDK header and EVENTS.md from this file. Adding an event or a table is one reviewed entry here.

sites.routine: the playback-increment builder 0x40004008(track, ping, start, end): STATIC, FLEX and PICKUP, and POLY8's tracks through it; lea -48(sp) and 44 bytes of saved registers put its track at 52(sp) here
head: .word 0xa1c0 | movclr.l %acc0,%d0: the increment, PTCH and RATE applied
asr.l %d6,%d0
tail: move.l %d0,36(%a3) | the track state's increment, read by the source fetch and the DSP voice command

sites.routine: 0x40006820(track): stops a track's voice and binds it fresh (clears its active byte and state, then 0x4000672c), interrupts masked; 8 or more does every track by calling this site once per track. Callers: the trig path 0x4000f518, the frame handler 0x4000d45a, the renderer 0x40008110, UI paths (0x40043c50 and five more)
tail: move.l 4(%sp),%d1 | stock's own prologue, its loads in another order
done: rts | the call returns as stock's does when it has nothing to do

sites.routine: MIDI IN chromatic note-on (the STANDARD map's chromatic block), once per listening track d2, a3 the message's note
MIDI IN chromatic note-off, once per listening track d2; a0 the track's held-note byte, a3 the note, d3 1 << track
tail: bne.s 1f | stock's bne.s, which cannot be copied

sites.routine: FUNC + LEFT/RIGHT in CHROMATIC mode: stock toggles its octave word 0x460d16fc (d2 the key)
the CHROMATIC drawer's common octave push (audio and MIDI reach it with the octave in d0)
boot: stock's sanitiser of the battery-RAM settings block, at its first test
tail: jmp 0x40010218 | its flags are the continuation's

sites.routine: project defaults (cold boot, no project, before a load, new project)
the CHROMATIC drawer picks the keyboard's octave
tail: jmp 0x40044970 | its flags are the continuation's

CHROMATIC key handler: the trig

CHROMATIC key handler: after the recorder call

the project loader's entry (a storing load)
the project loader's '#' line test
the project writer, after PATTERN_CHANGE_CHAIN_BEHAVIOR

the frame's track-record builder 0x40004bd4 (frame interrupt): for each track d4 (0-7) whose bit is set in STOP's tail-kill mask (0x8000184b, at 50(sp)), a2 the track's 64-byte record (0x80000110 + 512 x buffer + 64 x track), it tests the record's FX2 id (+56) against the three stock reverbs (0x14-0x16) and clears +24, +34 and +53 (FX2 SETUP slot 11) for them

events.when: the increment builder recomputes a track's playback increment (Q26, 0x04000000 = unity), after stock applied PTCH and RATE and before it stores it; when the builder reuses the stored increment no handler runs
events.context: the audio render, at interrupt level: short, no firmware call that can block, the EMAC kept as found
events.contract: Change *increment to change what the track plays at. Return nonzero to take the track: no later handler runs. The base stores *increment either way. The builder's d2-d7/a2-a6 are intact in a handler (a3 the track's 40-byte state, d6 the shift just applied) and must be kept, as C keeps them.
events.order: lower first, then module id. 10-29: a machine that owns its tracks' increment and takes them; 40-69: tempo and rate changes on other tracks.

subscribers.does: a POLY track's increment becomes its voices' tuning (poly_track_inc) and the DSP runs it at unity; it takes the track
subscribers.evidence: sdk/octabam/modules/poly8/polyphony.s poly_increment_shift; shared-machine-hooks.s mr_rate_hook sends POLY tracks there before any other module's rate_hook

subscribers.does: scales the increment by project tempo over the sample's tempo when REPITCH is on the track, clamped to 2x; d3 holds the sample tempo its rate_gate (0x4000406a) found in the same builder

events.orderEvidence: sdk/octabam/modules/poly8/composition.json replaces Repitch's 0x40004100 detour with POLY8's mr_rate_hook, which takes POLY tracks first and passes the others to rate_hook. POLY8 also forces a POLY track's live TSTR off (poly_config_tstr), so REPITCH never acts on one.

events.when: before stock stops a track's voice and binds it fresh; track 8 or more means every track, and stock then comes back here once per track
events.context: the frame interrupt or a task: short, no firmware call that can block
events.contract: Return 0 to pass. 1 drops this reset: stock does nothing and the call returns. 2 runs stock's reset at once: no later ev_voice_bind handler and no ev_voice_bind_run handler. Any other nonzero acts as 2. d2-d7/a2-a6 are the caller's and must be kept.
events.order: lower first, then module id. 10-29: a machine that renders voices itself and redirects the resets its renderer causes; 30-69: gates on ordinary tracks (mute modes).

subscribers.does: while POLY8 renders an extension voice, the reset stops that voice only (1); while it renders a primary voice, stock's reset runs at once (2)
subscribers.evidence: sdk/octabam/modules/poly8/shared-machine-hooks.s mr_stop_voice; polyphony.s poly_stop_voice, whose .psv_replay goes to stock without fresh_bind while rendering

subscribers.does: in OTFX-T and DT-T a single muted or soloed-out track's reset is dropped, so no new voice starts (a SIDE-CHAIN key track keeps it)

events.orderEvidence: POLY8's mr_stop_voice checks its renderer state before anything else, then Mute Modes' gate (its mr_mute_suppressed, a copy of fresh_bind's test, when fresh_bind is linked), and only then discards the track's extension voices (ev_voice_bind_run).

events.when: every ev_voice_bind handler passed: stock's reset runs next
events.context: as ev_voice_bind
events.contract: A notification: every handler runs; none can stop the reset. d2-d7/a2-a6 are the caller's and must be kept.
events.order: lower first, then module id; 10-90.

subscribers.does: discards the track's extension voices, held keys and queued presses, interrupts masked

events.orderEvidence: In POLY8 + Mute Modes the extension voices are discarded only when the reset is not dropped (mr_mute_suppressed returns first).

events.when: a module that silences muted and soloed-out tracks asks, once per frame while one of its silencing modes is on, which tracks' audio another module still takes as an input (a side-chain key); no stock site: the asking module calls the base's modwerk_raise_ev_mute_keep(), which returns every handler's answer OR'd, 0 with none
events.context: the frame builder (0x40004dbc), once per frame: short, no firmware call that can block
events.contract: Return the tracks whose audio this module reads while they may be muted: bit t for track t+1, bits 0-7; higher bits are ignored. Every handler runs. A silencer mutes these tracks as stock does (the post-FX cut) in every mode and lets their trigs and voices run, so the audio keeps reaching the module that reads it. d2-d7/a2-a6 must be kept.
events.order: lower first, then module id; every handler runs and the answers are OR'd, so the order does not change the answer. 10-90.

raisers.does: in OTFX, OTFX-T and DT-T, takes the answer's tracks out of the silenced set and gives them stock's own mute bit back (OT's post-FX cut); its trig, rebind, fresh-bind and trig-flag hooks let their trigs through (KEYMASK)
raisers.evidence: sdk/octabam/modules/mute-modes/patch_softmute.s p1_key (Session 116); natively the SC_KEY build reads SIDECHAIN_COMPRESSOR's KEY slots itself

events.orderEvidence: The answer is an OR: no handler can take or hide another's tracks. Natively the only provider is SIDECHAIN_COMPRESSOR's KEY (COMPRESSOR, FX id 0x18, page-2 slot 8: OFF or T1-T8), which the SC_KEY build of Mute Modes scans itself; here the module that owns the key answers for it.

events.orderEvidence: FM Synth bundles Tim Hastie's quantizer; FM's engine reads its own copy's mailbox, so FM's copy (40) serves before standalone Scale Quantizer (50). events.when: MIDI NOTE SETUP (double-tap SRC, or double-tap TRACK in MIDI mode) lists OFF and the contributed generators in its empty left half; a MIDI track running one shows that generator's pages on the MIDI pages it takes (always ARP; FUNC+AMP: the ARP page's second)
events.context: the UI task
events.contract: Contribute one struct modwerk_midi_generator (every field but abi, label and id optional, 0). Choosing it puts 'M' and its id in the track's arp step mask (Part 0x1822 + 2 t, high byte first), which stock's validator never reads and only ARP SETUP edits; stock's default there is ffff. On every change of generator the base first puts the track's arpeggiator back to stock's defaults (MODE OFF, every note 0), then calls the old generator's assign(t, 0) and the new one's assign(t, 1). While a generator runs a track it owns that track's 16 arpeggiator note bytes (Part 0x1832 + 16 t, each -64..63, the range stock's validator keeps), so the ARP page is always its own and FUNC+AMP never opens ARP SETUP there. Its pages show while no trig or scene is held (stock's then, so locks stay stock's); the base takes encoders A-F, YES and, on the second ARP page, NO there. Values behind the pages it takes stay stock's and keep their meaning (a NOTE page's NOT2-4 still add chord notes): set or show them itself. Layout A (owner, 24 October 2026): generators take SRC and AMP; FX1 and FX2 are kept for MIDI effects. A track whose id has no installed generator reads as stock.
